reasons: R01, R11, R18: receivables grew far faster than sales (DSRI 1.57, AR growth exceeds sales growth by 0.81, change in receivables 17% of average assets), a classic revenue-inflation signal, though partly explainable by acquired receivables (F22).

F22, F24, R04, R13: a major acquisition in the year drove 41% sales growth and a 92% soft-asset share; the business-combination critical audit matter indicates judgmental purchase-price allocation, goodwill and intangibles valuation.
F05, F25: an auditor change within two years combined with a voluntary accounting change in the same period raises concern about discretionary accounting choices.
F20, F26: incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS and emphasis on non-GAAP measures increase pressure and opportunity to manage reported results.
F03: no auditor attestation on internal control, so ICFR has had less external scrutiny.
R09, R17: Beneish M-score of -2.30 is below the -1.78 threshold and Dechow F-score of 0.81 is below 1.0, so the composite models do not flag manipulation.
R19, R08, R10: operating cash flow is about 7x net income and accruals are strongly negative, so earnings are well backed by cash, which argues against accrual-based earnings inflation.

F01, F04, F06, F07, F14-F19: no material weakness, going concern doubt, auditor disagreement, restatement, executive turnover, regulatory investigation, class action or covenant problem was disclosed.
